units.title: Almost-everywhere equality does not determine classical gradients
units.statement: It is false that, for every measure mu and every two real functions f and g, f=g mu-almost everywhere forces their classical Mathlib gradients to agree mu-almost everywhere.
assumptions: No regularity assumptions are imposed because the statement refutes an unrestricted congruence rule.
The counterexample uses the Dirac probability measure at zero.
The gradients are Mathlib's total classical gradients, not Sobolev weak gradients.

steps.title: Choose two representatives that agree at the atom
steps.text: Let mu be the Dirac measure at zero, f be the zero function, and g(x)=x. Almost-everywhere equality for a Dirac measure means equality at its atom, where both functions have value zero.
steps.lean: The proof rewrites the a.e. filter with ae_dirac_eq.

steps.title: Compute the two classical gradients
steps.text: The zero function has gradient zero. The identity function has derivative and hence gradient one at zero.
steps.lean: gradient_fun_const and hasDerivAt_id.hasGradientAt.gradient provide the two computations.

steps.title: Contradict the proposed a.e. gradient congruence
steps.text: If the unrestricted rule existed, applying it to these representatives would force 0=1 at the atom, a contradiction.
steps.lean: The claimed gradient a.e. equality is again reduced to its value at zero with ae_dirac_eq.

units.lean_statement: The theorem negates a universal implication over all real measures and all pairs of real functions. It uses an explicit Dirac counterexample rather than an axiom or meta-level warning.
units.lean_proof: Instantiate the universal rule with delta_0, the zero function and the identity; reduce both a.e. propositions to the atom and compute the two gradients.

sources.label: Chen, Chewi, Lu and Zhang, SPHMC v1, Lemma 4.17
sources.scope: The lemma states the restricted-Gaussian contraction and cites the prior relative-score proof; the obstruction concerns only the formal representative adapter.

sources.label: Lee, Shen and Tian, Lemma 2, equation (11)
sources.scope: Direct source for differentiating the explicit normalized density ratio and obtaining the affine score (y-y')/eta.

boundary: The theorem does not say the paper's explicit smooth score calculation is invalid.
It does not say Mathlib's particular llr has an incorrect gradient.
It does not rule out a full-support or absolutely-continuous result under added regularity, gradient transport from pointwise/local equality, an RGO-specific adapter, or Sobolev weak gradients.
It does not prove LSI, T2, Fisher evaluation, Wasserstein contraction or a main result.

tests.scope: The declaration is imported, type-checked and its axioms are printed.
